name: India–Pakistan
value: Airspace bans to 24 Nov; no strikes
summary: India–Pakistan airspace bans run to 24 Nov; Indus treaty dispute continues; no cross-border strike found to 10 Nov
state: Pakistan's ban on Indian aircraft runs until 24 Nov after its October extension (Gulf News), and India's suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty remains disputed. Searches on 10 Nov found no new cross-border strike, mobilisation or Line of Control clash. Unrest in Rawalakot, Pakistan-administered Kashmir, is an internal matter tracked under civil unrest.
for_you: Flights between and around India and Pakistan still face airspace closures and longer routings. Check with airlines and FCDO travel advice before travel.
rubric_hit: Treaty suspension and airspace bans persist; no cross-border strikes or mobilisation

sources.title: Gulf News — Pakistan extends airspace ban on Indian aircraft until 24 November

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
